item.title: With Single-Digit Temps Expected For Another Week, Lamont Extends CT’s Severe Weather Protocol Again
item.description: This is the longest stretch of consecutive days Connecticut’s Severe Cold Weather Protocol has been activated since 2015, when it was in effect for 34 days between January 26 and February 28.

item.title: 4 Lessons New England’s Grid Can Learn From Last Week’s Winter Storm
item.description: Extreme cold and lots of snow revealed the New England electric system’s strengths and weaknesses as the region debates how to build a more reliable, affordable grid.

item.title: CT Nonprofits Say $155M In Additional State Funding Needed
item.description: The group’s legislative goals also include repeal or reform of statutes that cap executive salaries below the market rate, leaving nonprofits with a limited talent pool to hire from; providing affordable health insurance options for nonprofit employees; creating student loan and tuition reimbursement programs; increasing access to affordable housing and supporting special education services through approved private special education programs.

item.title: More Than 30 States Have Cell Phone Bans During School. Will CT Join Them This Session?
item.description: Backers say the measure would protect student mental health, restore classroom focus, and foster genuine social connection during the school day.

item.title: CT Officials Tout New Liquor License Training Requirement In West Hartford
item.description: The initiative is administered by the Department of Consumer Protection, the state’s primary regulator of liquor establishments, and funded through the Department of Transportation, with additional funding and curriculum support from the Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services.

item.title: Incumbent Democrat Defeats Republican State Senator In Fairfield, Unofficial Results Show
item.description: Multiple news outlets are reporting that Christine Vitale defeated Tony Hwang by about 2,000 votes Tuesday.

item.title: CT Legislators Return For 2026 Session
item.description: Since this is an even year, Connecticut’s legislature will have a short session – only 13 weeks – that concludes May 6.

item.title: CT House Welcomes 2 New Members, Mourns the Late Kevin Ryan
item.description: Two new members of the Connecticut House of Representatives were given a warm welcome Wednesday during the opening session at the Capitol.

item.title: Transcript & Video: Lamont’s 2026 State Of The State Address

item.title: Lamont Draws On ‘Connecticut Common Sense’ In State Of The State Address
item.description: Drawing from Thomas Paine’s 1776 pamphlets, Common Sense, and The American Crisis, Lamont delivered a 40-minute speech with few surprises, and a handful of controversial moments.
